title: Deposits
body: Minerals in the rock leach one dissolved nutrient into the water beside them. Thionite leaks Sulfex, ferracite leaks Ferron, azoite leaks Nitrox, and halite leaks Osmolyn. The colored water sits against the mineral. A faint uncolored tail reaches farther, so the water still has a direction even where it looks empty.

A permease feeding from that water thins it. The mineral, and the slow mixing of the column, fill the scar back in. A cell that stays on one spot can pin the water there dark and leave a fading trail behind it.
